component_families.name: CHS — Categorical Header System. Ordinal + gold tick + category word (chs-stamp), display title (chs-title), italic descriptor (chs-descriptor), hairline rule with gold accent stub (chs-rule), plus FIVE named register variants
component_families.gap: THIS IS THE MAIN FINDING. Every section heading built so far (company profile's `.sec-head`, the legal derivatives' plain `<h1>`/`<b>` headings) is a parallel invention, not this system. The master already ships FIVE register variants for exactly this situation: `.chs--legal` (semibold uppercase title, medium-weight rule — literally named for legal content), `.chs--formal` (no descriptor, strong rule, navy category label — for formal/statutory headers), `.chs--plate` (compact numeral+title only, no rule — for dense reference lists), `.chs--minor` (inline compact heading, no rule — for sub-points), `.chs--toc` (smaller numeral, for table-of-contents rows). `.chs--primary` is the default full treatment already ported as company-profile's cover kicker style is NOT this — the profile's *section* headings (Overview, Capabilities, Governance, Engage) should have used `.chs--primary` or `.chs--formal`, and the legal derivatives' section headings should use `.chs--legal`. None of this exists yet in gssc-components.css or gssc-legal-components.css.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: The master's CSS is an append-only patch history (11+ sequential <style id="gssc-..."> blocks, each documented as superseding specific rules from the previous one). Any 'line-by-line' extraction must resolve the CASCADE — i.e. use the LAST rule for a given selector, not the first one found — exactly as the kernel's own 13_changelog.json discipline requires ('append-never-rewrite'). This audit did that (e.g. gate-refined supersedes .gate; colophon-docket supersedes early .colophon variants). Opus should do the same: read the whole file top to bottom and let later blocks win, never stop at the first match for a selector.

Every gap above is a MISSING REUSE, not a missing capability — the master already contains a correct, tested, doctrine-referenced component for each one. The fix is extraction and adaptation, not new design work. This matters for the 'premium' goal: the fastest path to premium is fidelity to what already exists, not fresh invention.

gssc-legal-components.css was deliberately built as a SEPARATE register per 09_legal_doctrine.formatting.pt_exception, and that separation is correct and should NOT be undone. The fix for legal derivatives is narrower: reuse gate-refined's STRUCTURE (field-by-field signature lines) adapted to Times New Roman/black ink, and consider whether `.chs--legal`/`.chs--formal` section-heading treatment (already literally named for this) should govern legal-document section headings instead of the plain bold headings currently used.
